goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
goldens.reasoning: G1's main point is that mixing floats with flexbox causes layout problems. C1 makes the same point: floats on flex items (float:left on .topic-avatar, float:right on the button) are ignored once .small-action becomes a flex container. G1's header .panel detail isn't covered, but the core concern overlaps.

goldens.comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions the invalid -ms-align-items prefix.

goldens.comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions that box-ordinal-group values must start at 1.

candidates: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 - Flex container ignores the float:right on the small-action button. `.small-action` is now a flex container, so the `float: right` on its `button` (and `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`) no longer applies to its flex items. `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`, so the button (for example undo or delete) now sits right after the description instead of at the right edge. Fix this by giving the button `margin-left: auto`, or by giving `.small-action-desc` `flex: 1`. The float rules can then be removed.
